could have been just another action rogue-like. What truly sets it apart is the inclusion of a time-based difficulty meter, which turns it into a rather intense survival game.
The goal of every level is as follows: look for a giant shiny red teleporter, then trigger it and survive waves of enemy spawns for a set amount of time (90 seconds on Normal mode). After the timer runs out, kill any remaining opponents and you can finally teleport to the next level. When you've completed five levels, you're given the option to teleport to the final stage or to revisit the previous ones.
This simple concept forces you to constanly find the right balance between rushing and exploring: you want to make the most of every level in terms of upgrades, but hang around for too long and the ever-increasing difficulty meter will make you pay. A typical playthrough can last an hour or more; and if you happen to die, no extra lives or continues: you're starting over.
The rogue-like elements are on point, with dozens of interesting items to discover and unlock as well as twelve character classes with very specific gameplay twists. Once unlocked, you can also choose to enable up to ten artifacts which alter the gameplay in a significant way. While not fully randomized, each stage has several different possible layouts which ensures every playthrough feels somewhat different.
A huge selling point for me was the option to play the game in local/online coop. Couch coop is great fun and quite playable, only requiring the players to stay relatively close to each other. Online coop gives the players more freedom and, for the most part, works very well; however, certain items (Chargefield) and possibly characters have a tendency to cause game-ending crashes.
This brings me to the flaws of
: a somewhat less polished technical side seems to be causing consistent problems for some users. Aside from very minor issues, it has been totally fine on my end (and the same goes for my friends), but I would definitely recommend testing the game as soon as you purchase it, and being ready to request a refund if you can't get it to work. A couple other nitpicks: the interface is rather bland and the platforming - not a huge part of the game, thankfully - can be infuriating.
On a more positive note again, the pixel art is quite decent, and the lore that unfolds through the monster and item logs paints a convincing universe. Last but not least, the soundtrack is
- whether you end up playing the game or not, you'll definitely want to check it out if you enjoy nice things.
tl;dr: a great blend of (hardcore) rogue-like and survival to enjoy on your own or with selected friends. Excellent replay value for the price.

Review is based on few hours of gameplay in co-op and solo.
First of all Dying light looks amazing  and the atmosphere is spot on. Reminds a lot like earlier first person zombie games but the free running element adds a lot more into the gameplay. The free running gets a lot more fun via perks for example you can vault off a zombie and dropkick another in mid air. You can jump from pretty high up without dying only if there is a convenient trash dump to land on.
Melee weapons tend to break quite fast and they can only be fixed 4-6 times depending on the quality of the weapon. Weapon modification is nice also, you can add electric damage, burning, toxic etc..or better handling or even durability.
Crafting is easy and you tend to find a lot of materials lying around to make medkits, molotov's, lockpicks etc.
When the city gets dark the game gets creepier, adds a bit more difficulty and different gameplay. Some of the quests require you to do them in the night and offer good rewards. You get a lot more experience when playing in night mode and have higher stats also.
Co-op is super fun with friends! There is nothing more satisfying than ganging up on zombies with human players. You can advance in the story mode in co-op just like in solo campaign.

Very interesting game and a lovingly-made homage to Diablo 1.
While the game is an ARPG, your character can only move in predefined paths. This takes some getting used to especially since the controls are still a bit clunky and unresponsive (I have almost died several times because my character was going in a direction it wasn't supposed to or it wasn't moving at all despite frantically clicking with the mouse). However, the voice acting, art style, graphics, and deck building mechanics are top notch. A lot of times the game feels less hack and slash and more action-puzzle (like Legend of Zelda) since a wrong move can spell either escape or utter defeat (and believe me, dying in this game really sucks). In this sense, it somehow becomes a rogue-lite.
PROS:
+ Exquisite art style, beautiful sound design, and a thoroughly immersive theme and atmosphere
+ Interesting combat mechanic (sadly marred by clunky mouse controls - hoping it gets fixed in the future)
+ High replay value due to procedurally generated dungeons
+ You feel that this game was made with just so much heart and love for the genre
CONS:
- Clunky/unresponsive movements
- Game difficulty ramps up too quickly for comfort. This is not a game you can just relax with and just hack and slash and kill monsters with like Diablo or Torchlight
- Dying equates to significant loss in cauldron rewards (which is a big deal as cauldron rewards award life or mana points)
- Some bugs (like my character disappearing all of sudden) but hopefully this gets ironed out when the game leaves early access
TLDR: Get it. Game is worth it even in Early Access.

The public events i have tried are fun and i have seen them in stuff like guild wars 2 and FFXIV but not a ton of others that i have played.  There are multiple ways to level rather then just killing mobs and such like alot of the ARPG's you can do public events as i said above and plenty of quest to follow along also.  The graphics i find to be pretty good but textures, shadows, and lighting are locked at medium when the rest goes to ultra and i found out the other day you can edit the config.ini file in game folder to force these to max there a a sticky in the discussions i seen.  and sound wise is good but i see in options it also has a Voice volume option but there are not voices in the game yet at least but again its early access so i'm sure this stuff will be added.  Now the item mall is like Path of Exile where its all cosmetics and mounts and a few convience items but no P2W aspects.  Class wise i have only played the engineer with priest sub and find it to be a great class and liking the attack skills that also heal and do a decent amount of damage so far i been soloing most of the dungeons until the level 15 range when the dungeons got a TON bigger and harder but do have to take it easy since you do get swarmed at times.

Overall: The game is awesome. I absolutely love it. You will need to watch a series or two of the show if you want to understand some of the in-jokes. However, this doesn't stop it from being a good game.
However, there are a couple of things that bother me, that also stop me from calling it an absolute masterpiece.
Positives:
-It feels like you are playing in a Southpark movie, were your character is the protagonist. It's all been very well designed.
-Very funny! (If you like politically incorrect/dark/gross-out humour, you will love this!)
-The characters are superb as always.
-Simple to understand as an RPG. Very standard (choose you role, beat and loot enemies.).
-Collecting is fun! There are all kinds of cool stuff to collect in the game.
-It's creative! As a fantasy, D&D styled RPG, it's been made very creatively. Items that you collect are imaginative (weapons will consist of household items, alien weapons and much more!) and even some of the various levels are creative (I don't want to spoil them).
-Lots of little side-quests that give you more than just the main story.
-Story is fun, it's very out there. (As you should expect from Southpark).
Negatives:
PLEASE NOTE FIRST POINT BEFORE PURCHASING:
-Some collectables are missable! There are some collectable items that you can only get during certain story missions and once you miss them, you will have to start a whole new playthrough to get a chance at them again. If you are an achievement hunter/perfectionsit like me, you may want to look up guides on the missable items in this game while playing.
Also your current collected items can NOT be transfered to a new playthrough, unfortunately.
-Most of the magic (fart) tutorials feel annoyingly difficult and aren't skippable. As far as I can see, they make it a lot harder than it turns out to be and they don't explain it very well. It's funny the first time, seeing as you need a tutorial telling you how to use your farts as a weapon, but it gets tedious.
Score: 9/10

Kane & Lynch: Dead Men is the single most under rated thrid person shooter. Period. It tries to be Ghost Recon meets GTA, but it ends up being something completely original. You don't play Kane & Lynch for the shooting and buggy as hell cover system; Gears of War does it a thousand times better. You don't play Kane & Lynch for some  mind-bending tactics; it ends up being more run n' gun than anything else. What you do play Kane & Lynch for is the story, strangely enough. The protagonists are a sociopath trying to save his family and a drug addict who slips in and out of uncontrollable mania. Sound interesting? That's because it is. The characters are where the game shines, but the plot is better than, well, any shooter I can think of. It may be a subpar game, but Kane & Lynch: Dead Men is one hell of a story.

Vengeance game review:
Vegeance game is being developed and published by 314 Arts, they are total of 6 people, the project is being made on Unity Engine, they've been working on this project since 02.05.2015 they strive to make this game without micro transactions and paid crates/drops. They listen to community and forum feedback and make changes based on the feedback they receive. There is to be 3 total game modes those are Single player, Coop and Multiplayer, time of writing this review only Multiplayer is ready, Multiplayer has 8 players a match though this is experimental number and will likely change over time, Multiplayer modes are: Team Death Match, Death Match, Global Thermal Nulear War, Push and Gun Game. In future they plan to add more game modes such as Capture The Flag. Coop will have Zombie mode which is wave suvival against hoards of Zombies, the other mode is Wave survival against enemies who will shoot at you. Single player is being planned, the developers have an idea what they will put in Single player wont say yet what it is. Later on in next few updates they'll have it ready to release.

Ideas:

Remember and keep in mind this is in Early Access there are still bugs that needs to be ironed out and more ideas to be added in this game.

Basically, it's Hearthstone, but with anime waifus. And who doesn't love anime waifus?
In all seriousness though, Shadowverse, for all intents and purposes, is a Hearthstone clone. However, this isn't necessarily a bad thing. The matter of the fact is that Hearthstone as it is now is incredibly unbalanced, and none of the new expansions seem to be coming close to fixing the issues the game has. Shadowverse meanwile, has a fresh start, and new mechanics to freshen up the game you're used to. You see, in this game, there's a mechanic which is called "evolving," and it allows you to turn your cards into more powerful versions of themselves about 2-3 times per game. Evolves bring a new level of strategy into the tried and true card battle formula, allowing for plays that could potentially change the tide of the game.
If you've played Magic: The Gathering, Hearthstone, or Yu-Gi-Oh before, and you want something new and exciting, at least give this game a try. It's not like other card games where you'll be paying hundreds of dollars just to make one good deck- they give you lots of free card packs when you start, and the ability to earn more in-game currency to buy more isn't that difficult. At the very worst, you'll waste a couple hours and find out this game isn't your thing. I hope to see you online sometime!

For Thief II, you could mostly just take my Thief Gold review, and then copy/paste all of the pros overtop of all of the cons. Thief II plays mostly the same as Thief Gold. Same graphics, same controls, same first-person view. What they did change, however, makes all the difference.
Thief Gold had a number of really fun missions featuring Garrett prowling around a house or opera hall or what-have-you, knocking out guards and discovering secret passages, and those were great. But it spent just as much time knee deep in zombies, apemen, giant bugs, bugmen, ghosts, confusing labyrinths, caves, and situations where you almost HAVE to fight your way out if you're not super-great at the game.
For Thief II, the devs looked at what players did and did not enjoy, and they made a game that is better in almost all respects. Save for a single Thief Gold-esque level with some apemen (which is rather forgiving compared to TG, and a fascinating level overall), there are only maybe a couple of any particular monster, and most of them are avoidable. The only new monster type I can recall gave me the biggest (and most enjoyable) fright of anything in either game. The majority of levels take place in sane man-made structures; homes, a bank, a surprisingly modern police station, and a few missions taking place across entire sections of The City. Thus the game now flows better, being less of a half-forced monster combat game, and more about sneaking around, bludgeoning unsuspecting jerks, and looting every last inch of each level.
As a result of the titular Metal Age, Thief II also now includes cameras, robots, turrets,  and a selection of new tools at your disposal, such as mines and flares - the latter of which you will absolutely need, as some parts of the game can be far too dark to move around in. It's possible this is an issue on my end, or it may just be part of the game. If it's the game itself, it is one of the very few problems introduced with this installment.
Also introduced, however, is a map. Though not always very helpful, it is often an invaluable tool, showing varied degrees of detail depending on the level and keeping track of where you've been and where you currently are.
While the final level is complicated and confusing, most of the rest of the game is a blast. One particular element of note is the interesting play on the penultimate levels of Thief Gold. Where in TG, the three levels leading up to the final one were repeat visits to locations you had already been in previous levels, in T2 the fourth-to-last level is ALSO a repeat visit to a location you had already been in Thief Gold, now taken over by the Mechanists. The next-to-last mission is, in fact, the same location as the third-to-last mission, which somehow manages to stay fresh and fun through both levels.
In the end, I heavily recommend Thief II if you enjoy stealth games. If you played Thief Gold but only sometimes liked it, I ask that you give Thief II a try instead, as it has ironed out most of the kinks. The only other thing I would like to note is that, like TFix for TG, Thief II is at its best when Tafferpatcher (a fan-made patch which improves resolution, textures, compatibility, etc.) has been applied.

One of the things a lot of people tend to forget is that this is an Early Access, meaning its still into development and has been released in such a way to improve the issues it has and get player feedback on it, so please keep this in mind!
For those that are lazy, have a reading disorder, don't like indept commentary or have the attention span of a goldfish (yeah who doesn't nowadays) here is a quick sum up:
Pros
- No P2W
- Dual Class system gives quite a fun factor experimenting with different setups and suite your  personal playstyle
- ARPG + MMO = Awesomeness
- WASD movement included (yeah like u care :D)
Cons
- Its into development?
So for those that want the full review, keep reading!
- No P2W, I see some people keep complaining about there being a cash shop while you pay for the game. They clearly didn't read any of the posts the devs made on this. So far all i'v read is nowhere near P2W and the developers really want to avoid this. However, as stated by the devs themself they need the cash shop to eventually still make income for development without having to sell DLC's, so guys be happy about this!
The following list is copied from their sticky about this subject (full story  can be read here)
Content of Loot Orbs (which are bought from the shop)
Exotic mounts, Cute pets, Exclusive costumes, Special furniture for your house, Experience and loot boosters, Inventory and bank expansions, Re-skill scrolls and Revive potions.
So in short, the only thing that can give you a small advantage is boosters, which only makes the time to level up and collect gold and such shorter.  No Gear or extra benefits that power up your character in any way, hence no P2W!
To add, there is a currency ingame collectable by doing daily achievments which lets you buy those same loot orbs.
- ARPG mixed with MMO equals awesomeness. Having an usual questline with a mainquest and sidequests along with public events that respawn on the map to complete, leveling your character alongside this huge world, which is still growing as the game gets developed, while meanwhile experimenting with many of the different combinations the class-system provides. Unlike many other ARPG's there is a Tank, Healer and DPS kind of roll. Which at this point of development doesn't have it real place yet, but is what the game is aiming for in the future.
To give an impression of what else to expect, think about different proffesions like mining (they actually released this today) blacksmith, gathering, alchemy, fishing! (as shown in one of the trailers ^^) and features like housing where you can decorate your house and hire sprites that help you out with your proffesions and level up on time. Also there is gardening and there are certain items to place in the house that give benefits like increased bonus xp when in the house (offline or online) that will be gained when killing monsters on your next adventure. As for the ARPG aspect, the feeling it gives Hack and Slash wise I like it! There has been previous notions of reviewers, one youtuber in particular I can't stand, I won't call out names.. that mentioned there being a delay in attacks. However since the steam early access release for me as an Europian player this has already been fixed (+ US server coming up soon!), only thing I occasionaly have is lag spikes which freezes the screen for a few seconds, which I am sure is being worked on and isn't a game breaker in this stage of development.
- Dual Class System, I personally really like this one, it gives you the ability to try out different combinations of classes to fit your playstyle and experiment with. The customization in general how attributes and skills work might be a little confusing at first . There are 4 different attribute types which influence your stats, think about increased crit, increased damage in a certain type (physical, holy, arcane, etc), increased block chance and so on. Stats gained from your gear increase these + they give some specific kind of increasements which seem to fit well together. Skills work as follow, you got one type of skill that regains your energy (usually used on the left mouse button) and another one (usually on the right mouse button) to consume without cooldown. The rest of the skills is with an usual cooldown.
- Great communication and response from the developers so far! I can keep this one brief, but from what i'v seen following the debates, they respond very quickly and nearly every time. Some times make we wonder if they work more on this game then looking at player feedback, JK* ^^
- WASD movement included, this might not be a biggy for most, but I personnaly might want to make a steam controller layout in the future and this will make it a lot easier and comfortable playing with one.
Cons
- ARPG aspect still has some work to do, besides the obvious fact a lot of content is still to come, which is not a con but a decision you have to make if you want to participate into helping the development of this game or rather wait for the finished product. In some occasions when you hold your left mouse (or if you use WASD) button to walk somewhere you get stuck, in which you have to struggle yourself out by jumping and clicking around. I'v also fell beneath the ground a few times into endless oblivion ^^ but there is a reset character button, so don't worry. And things like this are to be expected in an Early Access. As for the balancing between classes, its at this point hard to say since we aren't even at max level yet and can't see the full potential of the different kind of roles we play. All I can say is I can't wait to see! :D
- Skill System, its stated there is near unlimited character optimization with over 300 active and passive skills. I find this a bit overadvitised since about 2/3 of the skills are passive and only increase stats. Though there is still plenty of customization left with the way gear and stats work in general, combined with the active skills and dual class system, I am not sure how many skills each class has in total, since we can't become the max level yet, but how it works is a following. You have a linear active skill with 4 different subcategories split up between each other which are all a little different from each other, having two passive attribute increasements inbetween (which you can choose one of two, for example increased hit chance vs extra health points) that increase your total stat improvement. Which I also find quite falsy advertised on this idea of having so much different skills while in fact there a lot less then given the impression. Still despite all of this, like I mentioned before there is plenty of customization but I felt this needed to be mentioned.
Now i'v got my eye on this game for quite a while and decided to start a Youtube channel on this game (just been waiting for the steam early access release) so my opinion on this game might be a little biased towards the positive in some minds. But I choose to spend and invest my time into this game for multiple reasons. The environment makes me somehow give Diablo 2 vibes, oh the times I had with this game =D. The MMO aspect on an ARPG hell yeah! The traditional class roles, the customization, and the fact it gives the ability to play this with a steam controller is another plus for me. I wish everyone happy gaming times, and hopefully see u ingame :)!

Shadowrun Returns is an entertaining but short jaunt.  Invisible walls are everywhere while extensive exploration of environments is largely pointless.   The story script is very readable and compelling, even though there is little opportunity to alter events with dialogue or actions.  Music and sound effects are competent but could've used more variety.
Combat mode is entirely initiated by the game designers, even when there aren't any adversaries to fight.  Frequently whole areas will be in this mode which greatly slows down progress.   I also frequently encountered a "camera" bug (dragging my view inexorably to the upper left portion of the map) that could only be remedied with a save/reload.  Movement during combat can be muddy and there were many instances where I was trying to go to cover only to miss it if my click was a fraction off.  No backsies.
When Dead Man's Switch is finished (8 or so hours for most), there are plenty of fine community mods to play with.  Some are finished and still work, but others have been abandoned (sometimes to be reworked in Dragonfall) and are broken or incomplete.
8 out of 10

I went in knowing nothing about Shadowrun Returns and I came out chomping at the bit for more. Let’s get this going.
I – Story [10/10]
Shadowrun Returns is a turn-based RPG from Harebrained Schemes. While this game is open to mods and the Steam Workshop that can supply you with a plethora of campaigns, we will be dealing specifically with the core campaign “Dead Man’s Switch”.
After creating a character, the player takes on the role of a Shadowrunner who receives a pre-recorded video message from an old partner by the name of Sam Watts. The message was triggered by a “Dead Man’s Switch” Sam had had embedded within his body; ensuring that the message would send in the event of his death. The message states that Sam has 100,000 nuyen (the currency of the realm) that he will give to you as a reward if you bring his murderer to justice. Upon accepting the offer, the character sets off for Seattle and discovers that Sam is merely the latest victim in a slew of murders perpetrated by the Emerald City Ripper (a serial killer who has been surgically removing organs from their victims).
The player receiving help from an elven Shadowrunner named Coyote, who first asks the player for assistance in her private vendetta against those who make “Better-Than-Life” (BTL) chips. The Runners discover that the Ripper is an elf named Silas Forsberg; all of whose victims had a received organ donations from Sam’s mother at the time of her suicide. Once Silas has been dealt with, the player learns that he was hired to commit the murders by Jessica Watts, Sam’s twin sister, who blamed Sam for their mother’s death.
The Runners confront Jessica, but she manages to escape by sicking her goons on them. This leads to the discovery that  Jessica is a high-ranking member of the Universal Brotherhood, an international religious organization that attracts the impoverished and societal pariahs. The Runners investigate the restricted areas of the UB facility and discover that the Universal Brotherhood itself is merely a front for a cult trying to create a hive of supernatural insects. Jessica is revealed to be a shaman and one of the few who are aware of the Brotherhood’s true nature. She unleashes the supernatural insects that the Runners fight and are unable to kill. The team then flees, rescuing an elf named Mary-Louise who had been imprisoned and chosen to become “The Queen” of the insects.
Mary-Louise puts the Runners in touch with her boyfriend, a mysterious decker who goes by the alias “Baron Samedi”. Baron organizes a Shadowrun on Telestrian Industries to steal a sample of Project Aegis; a weaponized chemical capable of killing the insect. The Runners acquire the sample but, are captured while trying to escape and are brought to James Telestrian III. James, as it turns out, is Mary-Louise’s father and he decides to hire the Runners for a mission to use Project Aegis.
James arms the team with Project Aegis launchers and sends them back into the Universal Brotherhood compound where they infiltrate the hive and fight their way into the inner sanctum. Within the inner sanctum, Lynne (James’ sister) has volunteered to let the insect queen possess her body in place of the escaped Mary-Louise. The team disrupts the summoning by seriously wounding Jessica and killing many of the insects already residing inside the hive. The queen abandons Jessica and the player is given the option to execute her, arrest her, or let her die at the mandibles of the supernatural insects. Lynne survives the ordeal, but is arrested and sent to a mental institution.
The game winds down with the player discussing the events of the raid with James and the rest of the team. When the player tries to collect the money for bringing Sam’s killer to justice, Sam’s message asks the player to apologize to Jessica for everything that Sam put her through and admits that he never had the money to pay a bounty. What a d-bag right?
All in all, the campaign was pretty solid and it has a little bit of everything in it. The fact that I can download custom campaigns really sweetens the deal too. This is additionally great because Shadowrun has one of the most interesting science fiction/fantasy worlds I’ve ever encountered.
II – UI [8/10]
The user interface implemented in Shadowrun Returns worked very well with the turn-based gameplay. There’s not a whole lot you’ll need to learn that you can’t figure out for yourself (which is good because there is no tutorial). There’s also no minimap available on screen and I felt that a minimap would definitely have been useful for both navigational and strategic purposes. I also feel like the menus could have used a few tweaks here and there, especially the skill tree tab where you spend your karma points.
It’s easy to find what you need to be doing in the game; the compass provided for you in the upper left corner is a bit screwy, but it won’t make a ton of difference. Keeping tabs on your party’s health bars is a cinch and you’ll have all the information you need for combat at your disposal during combat.
III – Gameplay [9/10]
The gameplay was simple and enjoyable. With turn-based games (especially RPGs) it doesn’t take much before learning the game is like trying to memorize a college textbook. Class customization is very free form is that’s the sort of thing that you’re into or you can select a pre-made class. Character classes and skills are the most complex aspect of gameplay, but you’ll figure it out as you go and you’ll be comfortable with it in no time at all. The left mouse button does all the work, (no right-clicking or using hotkeys to preform actions in game is necessary). My only real complaint was the lack of a looting system.
Honestly, there isn’t too much to say on this subject.
IV – Content [6/10]
Story-wise, by the time you finish the campaign you’ll feel like you’ve read an entire novel. There is a lot of story content packed into the quest lines in the game. However, there isn’t nearly as much content when it comes to actual items and aesthetic character customization. There are several “tiers” of items that gradually unlock for purchase as you get further into the game. You may be able to squeeze some more gear out of user-made content, but I don’t know for sure as I haven’t gone into the workshop yet much myself. Also, over time, enemies feel very repetitive as far as visual diversity goes. You’ll be fighting a limited group of baddies throughout the game. That may bother you or it may not, but I found it to be a bit boring towards the end.
As far as character customization is concerned, there are several playable races and a vast amount of options when it comes to designing a class, but, when it comes to how your character looks, your options become fairly scant.
V – Visual [7/10]
The artwork of Shadowrun Returns is absolutely gorgeous. The actual graphics, on the other hand, are somewhat mediocre. For a game that released in mid 2013, the graphics seem rather dated and polygonal. Does this detract from the gameplay? No. But, it isn’t all that aesthetically pleasing.
VI – Audio [9/10]
I loved every last track of music that played in Shadowrun Returns. I was hooked from the moment the theme on the main menu started going. It’s solid, atmospheric music and it really enhances the experience as a whole. There were no voice actors for this one as all of the game’s dialogue is conveyed through text. Sometimes, a lack of vocalized dialogue can be a hindrance to a game, but, in this case, it made it feel more like a novel (as I mentioned above).
VII – Overall [8.2/10]
Overall, Shadowrun Returns is a pretty good game.

First and foremost, this should be a free to play game. You have to use real money to actually get the ease of life things in the game. Inventory expansions, skill/stat resets, mounts, etc. I'm literally so sick and tired of paying for a game and then expected to pay more just to reset my skills? It makes no sense to me, but they took my money so jokes on me. There's also really nothing new with this game. It's a water downed version of Devilian. Although, I don't know if Devilian added housing. Regardless, the housing is just a cheap diversion from the already cookie cutter game. I'll just go into the pros and cons from here...
Pros:
- Has a decent amount of content, kinda.
- Graphics are ok.
- Public quests can be refreshing from the mundane linear quests.
Cons:
- Still have to pay (again) for cash shop things that should come free since you have to buy the game from the start.
- No storyline at all, just kind of floats you through the game.
- Very linear gameplay.
- Combat is poor. Massive lag in between actions, no fluidity.
- Crappy chat options (seriously, things like this should be a long forgotten thing of the past).
- The 60+ dungeons that they advertise are pretty dumb, you can run most of them solo and they're not really dungeons per se.
- The classes are all lopsided in pvp. Needs a lot of love in that department.
- Massive lag, this game is EU based, so be warned.
- All in all, there's nothing new here and it just seems like a money grab from the devs.

Despite its simple graphics, Risk of Rain is a wickedly good roguelike and you should own it.
The game features an assortment of classes, which gradually unlock as you default challenges within the game.   The classes change how you interact with the levels, and provide additional replayability on top of what is already a compelling game.
Basic gameplay involves simple combat, exploration, and tradeoff choices in how to spend your resources.  There are boatloads of upgrades of various rarities, many of which are stackable which can be anything from a minor boost, to a hugely impacting laser sweep or exploding enemies.
There's a constant time pressure, as the random encounter difficulty scales up the longer you play.  So while you may find yourself tempted to just park and farm on a particular low level, even that will eventually become uncomfortable, and the next level will be brutal because of it.  You either rush forward, and content yourself with fewer items but a better your level : monster level ratio, or take it slow and fight better equipped against harder foes.  It is well balanced and makes for a good tradeoff.
Each level type contains a distinct set of enemies, with randomized placement and individual feature tweaks.  The game has lots of challenges which unlock new dropped items, gameplay modifiers (usually tradeoffs that you can decide to play with), and classes.
I admit I'm one of those people who generally feels a game is complete when I've unlocked every achievement for the game.  Risk of Rain is one of those games that even after I have long since done this, I still find myself picking it up to play randomly regardless.

Well, that was quite the adventure.  I almost don't know where to begin.
Stick of Truth is a turn-based RPG, specifically more of the JRPG variety despite taking a few notes from the WRPG games.  But when I say turn-based, I don't mean that you simply click on the enemy you want to fight exactly one time and watch an attack happen.  This type of turn-based is much more interactive where you have to press certain buttons in a certain fashion for attacks to connect properly and deliver the most potential damage.  For example, when using Butter's Hammer of Storms ability, you have to click a button when the lightning strikes his hammer, or else the attack will fail and you'll perform a pitiful amount of damage to your target.  Then also, this same combat mechanic is used for blocking or quick time events, allowing you to either lessen the damage you receive or outright avoid it in certain situations.  It's very similar to the Mario RPGs in that regard, making it very interactive and forcing you to pay close attention.  Thanks to this, combat never really felt boring to me.
The world of Stick of Truth is also extremely fun to explore.  I really did feel like the city of South Park was created to its fullest, giving me access to just about every location that was known in the show.  Most of the city is accessable right away for the most part, though there are a few places you can't reach until you unlock certain abilities.  But the game isn't harsh by allowing you to stay lost, for your menu will always tell you where you need to go and have a giant exclamation point over it on your map.  It even does the same thing for any side quests you're doing at the moment.  Now I know you might be worried about having to walk EVERYWHERE in this huge town to accomplish your many tasks, but thankfully, this game provides instant transport, reducing that monotomy.  It is such a huge time saver.
The plot of the story, as you can probably guess, is pure comedy.  I mean, it's South Park, what do you expect?  As the story progresses, you'll find yourself laughing at just about everything in the game, whether it's for the ridiculous dirty humor or the jabs at the JRPG genre.  And yet, despite the humor, there really is a certain kind of epic feel to the story.  Yeah I know its just a bunch of fourth graders LARPing and blowing everything out of proportion, but I'm serious when I say I felt this game had some genuinely awesome moments.  Rescuing Princess Kenny from one of the elves that was♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥her was one fine example.  Well pretending to♥♥♥♥♥♥her by jumping up and down on the bed with Kenny tied up next to him and just standing there (what you thought I was serious?). So to rescue her, you have to break into the bedroom, climb up some shelves, then rip the ceiling lamp dangling above the elf out so that the wiring is all loose so that it resembles a zipline.  Then you slide down the wire and with your momentum, ram right into the guy to knock him out and break the whole bed and get Kenny out.  It's so stupid and childish, but it was awesome at the same time.
And the music certainly helps give off that epic feel too.  The entire soundtrack sounds like something out of Skyrim or Lord of the Rings, which is just amazing and really helps add to the atmosphere of the whole thing.
With all that said, this game isn't for the sensitive.  Stick of Truth is merely South Park in video game format, meaning that the offensive and vulgar humor is still all there in its purest form.  And this time, absolutely nothing has to be censored (unless you're getting the European or Australlian version).  Some small spoilers here, but there is a part in the game where you have been shrunk down and there's a boss battle in your parent's bedroom on their bed.  While your parents are there.  Having sex while you are battling the boss underneath them.  With porno music playing the background.  Don't even get me started on the quick time event that occurs during the fight.  I feel bad for the poor suckers who played this in front of their sensitive friends/Twitch viewers and never saw it coming.  And only worse things happen, as hard as it is to believe.  But hey it's South Park.  I wouldn't expect anything less.  Especially since one of the achievements is even named "Too Far" and requires you to do something really messed up.
This was Trey Parker and Matt Stone's first attempt at becoming involved in a South Park video game.  There were previous South Park games, but none of them had Trey and Matt actively working alongside the development team.  And boy, can you tell that those two had put everything into this game.  I couldn't even begin to name all of the references to the show that they put in here.  It's simply impossible.  This game, is without a doubt, one of the most entertaining and hilarious games I've played in a very long time and I applaud those two for all of the effort they put into it.  Despite it being only about 10-20 hours long, kind of easy at times, and awkward to watch other times, they did a fantastic job.
Here's looking forward to the Fractured But Whole.
And whatever you do, DO NOT PLAY THIS GAME WITHOUT HEADPHONES.  It is extremely NSFW and your parents will probably disown if they see you doing even half of the stuff in the game.

This game is a good addition to the Revelation series, with new guns, zombies, and the traditional Resident Evil theme we all so enjoy with a great story with likeable characters. However, the direction Capcom has been taking the Resident Evil series still feels fairly shallow. Though the singleplayer is very good, the replayability is detearing simple because you will find your self at certain parts of the campaign in you mind thinking 'Oh my god, I need to do this annoying part again.' Beyond that, the DLCs and different ending do give some incentive to play the singleplayer a little longer.
DLC, DLC, DLC, and more DLC. As we as gamers have become all too fimilar with the dreaded DLC over the years, the current marketing schemes by developers will not be changing anytime soon or in the near future. Therefore, its hard to give a game a negative point based on something that has become 'common practice'.
Moving on to the other half of the game called Raid Mode. It is a mode that most player migrate too after finishing the campaign is the same scripted horde modes that we have been seeing since earlier titles of Resident Evil. Though many of us Resident Evil fans have been waiting for more depth in term of the Raid Mode nothing has changed at all over the years. The same shallow horde mode still endures with no incentive but to grind for weapon upgrades which make your guns stronger so you can... You guessed it... grind for more weapon upgrades. New to Revelations 2 is character customizations, though this does ad a little more depth to the game it also adds more of the grinding, playing the same high end maps over and over.
There are more costumes and maps going back to RE6 int he game which do add more flavor, but at the same time a lot of us players still miss characters and costumes we all come to love, Such and Chris, Jessica, and who can not love Jill's older costumes?
I give this game a 7/10 as a Average game, still superior to RE6, but lacks any major improvements over Revelations 1.

I want to start by saying its a great game.
Maybe not 60$ great though, as it feels incomplete in many ways, all thoughout the game I find things undeveloped, limited or buggy in small but annoying ways.  A quick rundown of the good & bad;
Pros
- Fun sandbox with fluid parkour system, good ragdoll physics and loads to explore.
- Great graphics and video effects (including an amazing amount of gore and dismemberment done really well - that could be a con though).
- Excellent music and sound effects (contact sounds are really satisfying and visceral).
- Large community which will hopefully be able to produce mods for the game to increase its replayability.
Cons
- Canned story, dialogue writing, and a few types of random encounters and events (not necessarily awful, but nothing new, and not an outstanding example).
- An incredibly simplistic melee system with some additional depth (not much) added through skill gain.
- Very basic item system with artificial variance introduced with prefixes but many reused models and a modding system that has some appearances of complexity but really equates to four effects added singularily or in combinations along with sockets that can increase the 3 basic attributes every melee weapons has.
Ranged weaponary is even more limited with no modifications and the same few weapons given with absolutely no vairance other than color rarity.
Conclusion
The game is fun, and thats what really matters, it is satisfying cutting zombies into pieces, curb stomping them when they are down, and jumping around the city like spider-man (even moreso when you unlock the grappling hook).
Still, when your running around your almost certain to find some immersion breaking moments; ranging from bugs to bad writing.
If your on the fence I would definitely suggest waiting for it to go on sale, though with the product they have delivered and the promise of an active modding community I don't regret my purchase at full price.

RE Revelations 2 is a step in right direction for the RE franchise.  While it is still closer to the "action-oriented" feel of RE 4 than the original trilogy, the pacing is such that it feels more like a survival horror game than either RE5 or RE6 ever managed.  For the optimal experience, I recommend starting fresh on the "Survival" difficulty.  I found that it made the enemies deadly enough and ammo important enough to put the "survival horror" feel back into the game.
The level-design is mostly narrow corridors and tight rooms (as opposed to arenas where dozens of enemies charge you at once, although there are a few moments like that still).  Ammo is also limited and enemies can take a lot of damage if you don't target their weak points, so it forces you to play deliberately and do sneak attacks where you can rather than rush in like Rambo.  You will also have to dodge attacks with the dedicated dodge button as the level design will put enemies right up in your face, so it helps to make the game feel more intense and suspenseful.
There are still some strange aspects to contend with.  Each chapter is actually split into a Claire portion and a Barry portion which takes place 6 months after.  While this makes for some interesting storytelling as things you do in Claire's portion may affect Barry's portion, it also means that much of the level design is repeated.  Barry is also better armed and seems to have more health, so it ends up feeling that his sections are easier even though they are the second half of each chapter.  This gives the game an uneven progression as my Claire was always low on ammo/supplies while my Barry had so much extra his inventory was full.
The NPC companions are not the smartest, although they are usually not a liability.  While you can switch to control them at the press of a button, the problem is that you can game-over if the main character dies while you are controlling the NPC, and the AI is not great at avoiding damage.  Thus, you end up switching to your NPC character to use them as bait, rather than treat them like a proper character.  This is especially funny in Barry's campaign as his companion is a little girl, and yet you just casually send her into the middle of the zombies to get mauled while you snipe them from afar, or throw a fire bomb in the middle while she's still there.
An added bonus is Raid mode which is just a bunch of challenges to kill enemies.  You earn currency to buy new guns and mods, as well as XP to level up your character and build skills.  Every once in a while you have to protect some targets or get through the level in a certain time limit, but for the most part it is just mindless killing.  The game does try to spice things up by introducing enemy mods such as making them explosive, extra fast, or even invisible, but generally speaking it is not that tactical.
One of the most compelling things about Raid mode is actually that it teaches you how much damage different attacks do.  For example, I learned the weakness for a main story enemy only after I had already beaten the game because I saw that hitting a very specific spot in Raid mode did massive damage.  While there's not much depth to it, it is enjoyable enough to give a spin even if you don't have the patience to unlock ever stage and max out your character.
The DLC is lackluster and I don't recommend it.  The Moira DLC is basically just two glorified arena fights separated by supply gathering sections.  The arena sections don't even have proper level design as the game just warps you from room to room as you kill enough enemies.  The Natalia DLC is basically a crappy MGS simulator where you sneak to avoid enemies.  Neither adds much to the story and are not fulfilling in the gameplay department.
Overall though, I found the main game and Raid mode entertaining enough to feel satisfied for my $20.  While it's not a GOTY by any stretch, RE Revelations 2 did enough to give me hope for the next RE installment (especially after the letdown that was RE6).

After finishing System Shock 2 in 1999, The geniuses at Looking Glass Studios would set out to create a sequel to their most successful franchise. It would sadly be their last ever game as financial problems would see the studio close 2 months later.
Thief 2 is everything you could possibly ask for in a sequel; tighter and much larger level design, deeper exploration of the characters, a tighter and a more coherent atmosphere and an enthralling story of an unlikely alliance solving a twisting and evolving mystery that threatens to destroy The City and beyond.
Once again, Garrett is the unlikely hero of the tale. Stealing to survive and slinking through the shadows are a daily fact of life for him; Getting to the truth, whilst stopping to line his pockets along the way.
You'll be exploring nobleman's estates, police stations, banks, cathedrals and even The Thieves' Highway. All the while, the atmosphere and storytelling will keep you on your toes and keep your mind sharp. The environments in Thief 2 are much bigger and much more detailed than the first game and gone are the vast majority of undead, haunted crypts and tombs the first game contained.
You'll also have some new gear to play with in Thief 2; Slow-fall potions, expensive and rare invisibility potions, flash mines and 'The Eye', which I won't go into much detail about, as well as others.
Thief 2 is also more challenging than the first game. Higher difficulty levels will, in some cases, require you to leave very little or, in one case, zero trace of your presence behind in one or two levels. This will require you to think ahead even more about what to expect; a tense but rewarding experience.
This game the peak of the Thief series so far, the graphics are much improved over the first game and the story, whilst having a satisfying conclusion, left the door wide open for a Thief 3 that would never arrive from the studio that started it all.
So Adiós Looking Glass. You created amazing experiences, stories and gameplay long before it was the norm in gaming as we know it today and even now, studios are still playing catchup to you.

If you think whether you should buy this game or not, stop it right now. Because if you're into Hack'n'Slash, dungeon crawlers, and action RPGs, Book of Demons IS the perfect game for you.
I got excited when I first saw the screenshots drifting somewhere on the Internet, but at the same time I knew it might be "just another clone." However, after I met the developers at a Polish event and played the Pre-Beta Demo, I knew I had to have this game on Day 1.
I love the paper craft art design, music and voice acting. I also enjoy the fact that instead of regular items you have these CARDS that you can switch and upgrade whenever you want. Because of this, the possibilities to play your character are endless. Well, maybe not "infinite," but you can try multiple builds with the same character. For instance: AoE build, Single-attack Glass Cannon or Bomb thrower - just to name a few.
Learning curve is great too. Our class is well-balanced even if you sometimes have problems defeating certain levels. After those 8 hours I know, that if I can't defeat an enemy I just have to switch build and use all the cards I have to progress in the storyline.
Overall, a must-have for any fan of the genre. But if you've never played aRPGs and Dungeon Crawlers, Book of Demons might help you change your mind. Good luck!

Review:
So I've played a good 60+ hours in the game now and here's what the game brings to my list of criterias on what makes a good arpg for me:
1. Combat 4/10
Good animation quality on spell effect but, there is a disconnect between the interaction of the impact from the animation of your char and what happens to the mob. At first it did not grab me since the animation of the spells are well done and represents what you think should happen and the reaction on screen. But with the disconnect between these two we have floaty combat. Without the impactfull, meaty combat I can't enjoy this game in the longrun, it's that important to me. Some other game examples from my perspective that have floaty combat are POE, Titan Quest and what I've seen from Grim Dawn(it's the same engine as Titan Quest). But I think this feeling is mostly due to that I love melee characters. If they feel floaty they often end up feeling like a caster even though your not. So if you like casters you will probably not have an issue. Whether this represent good combat to you, thats another thing but for me it's the dealbreaker.
Combat pace there's nothing wrong with. It might be slower than say Diablo but its cohesive with the rest of movement in game and cooldowns on skills and interractions with your environment and smashing mobs in large droves really make the dopamin pop!
2. Cohesive and Emersive aesthetics 8/10
Graphically it fits my bill. Everything fits well together and pallete never goes crasy like most Korean mmos that often brakes immersive with the feeling that your living in a colorbook rather than a medieval/fantasy world. But this doesn't. It feels medieval/fantasy and is very reminiscent of Neverwinter Nights, tho not as grim.
3. Skills and Gear 8/10
Multitude of skills and combos that have a large variation due to the dual-class system and large open skill trees were you with every point also buffs a passive skill. These interract well with a large pool of random stats that all gear can have. With a rune system that can extract, replace or add stats to said item plus a reroll option on mainstats on gear, a skillpoint setup that actually matters, not like paragons in D3, that everyone can wear all armor with up and downsides, theres an insane ammount of customisation that never looses touch with it being a understandable mmo.
If this doesn't bother and you than you should invest and support the developers and try it out because there are so much more in this game like housing, trading, pvp, dungeons, questing, story, crafting, fishing, guilds, Zone-events etc, that is going to make this a great game for some.
The above 3 large criterias are what make good arpg for me. If your the same, wait for full release, that is my suggestion, since I have a feeling it might go free to play and will make it east and cheap to try.
Will I be back for full release, absolutely, I really whanna see were this game ends upp and how the game develops after early access :)

One of my favorite games since joining Steam, Lego Marvel Super Heros is one of the best lego games in terms of both, story, free play, and its overall design. That is not to say though, that it doesn't have its fair share of problems like every lego game does. While these problems do hinder the gamepaly a bit, they can be overcome with some simple adjustments that I will mention in an upcoming guide. But moving on from that, the story is both based upon the movie franchises continuety and its own, givign the impression that it could be a branch off from said films. It also does something that the films either cannot, or have yet to do, and that is bring in (almost) all of Marvels heros and villains together and no Sony, Fox, or Paramount to stop them from doing so. With that being said, the game mechanics are nice and simple, characters have a unique range of abilities and can speak very truely of their original comic book counterparts. But playing with a friend in two player mode can be a bit tricky if your using an xbox controller and they a keyboard or vice-versa, as whatever keys you've binded to your personal liking will sometimes reset themselves to their default state. A minor nitpick but one that can be fixed by buying another conrtoller or using the default keys. Now as for free play, I will say that there isn't much vaule in it, not like with older lego games such as Star Wars: The Complete Saga and Indian Jones: The Original Adventures, and I feel that this takes away some of the free roaming aspect that I expect in lego games, but at the same time, gives us something new and unique to see. With all that being said, I highly recommend this game to those who are both a fan of Marvel, Lego, and enjoy these games growing up on the Gameboy or who have little ones who've taken an intrest in video games. Despite crashing at times, a few bugs (or should I say ants) and some missing peices, this is a really great game.

So, looking at the game on steam store page, I debated for about 2 hours to buy this. I love hack and slash/ diablo like games. The loot grind calls my name. But the artistic direction threw me off of an impulse buy. But I am so glad that I picked it up.
So, this game is the first in a 7 game series to pay homeage to old pc gems. This is obviously based on the first Diablo game. How did they do?  Fantastic. This game is just great. I dont feel like i am playing diablo at all, but I can see the inspiration. That is what makes me so happy. If I want to play Diablo, I'll just go do that. But this game is unique in its art direction and game mechanics in a great way.
So how was my experience? Well, I thought I woud write my review after an hour-hour and a half. At around the point where people debate refunds from steam. So what am I thinking? Well, after about 20 minutes in the game, a bit of world building an a small dungeon later, I encounter one of this games best features, IMO.
So, I am a husband and a PhD student working on his disertation in post-quantum crypto. So my gaming hobby doesnt get all the time i wish it did. But, sometimes I ahve 15 minutes of nothing and would liek to hop into a game. I cant try to get back into a game like witcher3 where I would barely get into a side quest. Not enough time for a round of my moba or mmo of the month. Yet, Book of Demons has a beautiful solution. So, when you go to enther the dungeon, after your first one, you encounter a slider bar, which changes the lenth of dungeon you can enter, with a time estimator. This time estimator will learn based on your previous dungeon runs to become more accurate. This feature alone made me go to the main website and purchase the founders bundle for all 7 games. (I dont expect this feature in all 7, but this game just made me too happy to not want to throw my money at R2G)
So, now when I have 10 minutes or an hour, I can choose a dungeon of appropiate length, and have a blast with the card based ability/armor/loot system. I know there is a good amount of humor and movie/game references in this game, which I look forward to finding. Also, for achievement hunters, this game has 150 i believe? I read that in a forum post, so dont quote me on that.
Anyway, sorry for the long review, but just a fantastic job Return 2 Games. I look forward to the final product of Book of Demons and the other 6 installments of your series. I gladly throw my money at you for your hard work and will continue to be a happy customer.

I got the premium edition for $20 last February, didn't play it until Septermber, and beat it back in October with 100% completion. The game was meh. it felt more like an updated Arkham City than the final grand chapter of the Arkham series. The Arkham Knight characrter was a dissapointing villian who's identity was obvious. He also suffered from Bond Villain Stupidity at one point. I thought Scarecrow was OK though and I liked the Joker hallucinations that go on through out the game. A lot of the side missions just felt repetative with you just doing the same thing over and over. Two Face? Go to a bank being robbed by Two Faces' thugs, take them down before they steal all of the money, rinse and repeat. Fire Fly? Go to a building that's on fire to find him there, chase him around the city in the Batmobile until the fuel in his jetpack gets low, fly out and tackle him to the ground, damage his jet pack with a quick time event, he flies away, rinse and repeat. Penguin? Follow a truck full of money his thugs are taking to a warehouse, beat up everyone in the warehouse, blow up the stash there, rinse and repeat. I could go on. Some of the side missions were also very dissapointing story wise with the most dissapointing one for me being the one with the villian Hush. Remember how his side mission ended on a cliff hanger in Arkham City with him reconstructing his face to look just like Bruce Wayne by using parts from the faces of the people he murdered? Were you looking forward to finding out what he was going to do in Arkham Knight? Prepare to be very dissapointed.
.....that's it. That's all that happens.-_-
A lot of the strory DLC is mediocre and just feels like they ripped it from the base game to sell separetely. The one I lked the most is Mr. Freeze's story. The gameplay and action is good and the story is tragic, satisfying, and ends on a tear jerker concluding Mr Freeze's story of trying to find a cure for his wife. Batgirl was OK I guess but $10, the price of her story pack at the time I bought the game, was too much for just an hours worth of content. And Batgirl is the longest DLC story pack out of all of them. Ra's al Ghul's was OK too.
The few boss battles in this game, If you can call them that, are a joke. Like many things in this game the "boss fights" are repetative with no challenge. You simply trigger some quick time events where you do the same moves over and over until the boss is defeated and the boss is usually surrounded by mooks. The exceptions to this are the Arkham Knight boss fight, The Riddler boss fight, and the
boss fight. For me the Riddler fight was the best becasue it was challenging. Unfortunately
fight is just a tank battle and an easy one which was dissapointing to me because I haven't played Arkham Origins. So when I went to fight him I was looking forward to it. All he does is fight you using the suped up tank the Arkham Knight used.
A lot of people complained that the Batmobile is used to much but I didn't have a problem with it. I don't like it or dislike it. It's just part of the game for me.
Finally the secret ending you get after getting 100% completion just isn't woth all of the work you have to do to get it. It's short and should've just been an after credits scene. you're better off just looking it up on youtube.
About performance: Even after all of the updates I still got studdering and long freezes that would last for several seconds. The freezing would usually happen after I exited the map for some reason. Luckily the studdering and freezing wasn't freqent enough to make the game unplayable. There was also a certain point in the game where the game kept crashing. Fortunately all I had to do was verify the game cache and Steam found 14 missing files. Steam downloaded the missing files and that fixed the problem. Those are the only performance problems I had.
As I write this review the game is $20.00 which is a great price to get this at. I wouldn't bother with the DLC except maybe Batgirl's Story pack, A Matter of Family, and Season of Infamy for the Mr. Freeze and Ra's al Ghul's side mission.

It's so very lonely up here.  Everyone stays at their station, all the time.  Being together means having to work, or needing to heal the egregious wounds of your routine.  Nobody says a word.  Nobody sleeps a wink.
You would think in the event of an intergalactic crisis there would be somewhere you could go,  some escape.  There isn't.  Your short life demands to be lived.  Damned Rebels. They'll catch you, no matter how fast.  They'll find you,  no matter how lost. They'll kill you, with a yawn.
Fuel is everything.  Buy it all.  Weapons are meaningless, without the power to run them.  Crew is essential, as losses are commonplace.  Humans are worthless.  Drones are ideal.  Teleport aboard, and fight like men - or ion blast their oxygen,  and wait them out.  Time is your only ally,  and the music is your only friend.

The quality is great (I think it's on par with the blu-ray, since it pretty much matches the release date, audio and video are crisp and perfect.)
As for the movie itself, it's grand. It's back to the classics, with Yugi and the gang caught up in another situation that they must contend, the fate of the world resting on the card game, once again.. The artstyle is incredible, the dub is fantastic(all the old cast, though unfortunately Maddie Blaustein could not return as the voice of Solomon Mutou... Rest in peace.).
For the first time in the series the duels are done with 8000 life points, just like in the actual TCG, but for good reason, they're using some of the strongest meta decks (that were available at the time of the movie's original release) you finally get to see a taste of what modern Yu-Gi-Oh! is like without being held back by plot, and taking 3 episodes to deal 4000 damage.
It's a great throwback and feels like a total love letter to long time fans of Yu-Gi-Oh! while being greatly entertaining, feeling like a great conclusion to the classic franchise as we bid farewell to them once again. More or less they kept the dialogue pretty similar to the original JP version, 4K definitely aren't censoring as much as they used to, which is great; considering I feel this is one of the better plots in the Yu-Gi-Oh! franchise even though it's still pretty insane, as long as you're familiar with the series it's pretty easy to follow.
Also it's worth noting that this includes the japanese audio track AND english audio track, although store page says english only!

TOO HARD!!! sucks! It really pains me to write this negative review like many Others on here....too bad I didn't listen to them!!!
If you enjoy KF1, just keep playing that, and Pass on the sequel..... in KF1 you can just set it on "Easy", and just mow down monsters and have fun, no pressure until you get to the Patriarch...but KF2, the lowest setting is "Normal", which isn't too bad, until you get to Round 6....then it just gets WAAYY too crazy, especially for New Players. You can empty magazines into a crowd of monsters and you barely get any kills. It feels like your bullets do Zero damage unless shot at incredibly tight groups...just annoying. I mean that was the FUN part about KF1, is the "spray and pray" strategy in the "heat" of the battle...just doesn't apply anymore...so no perfectly planted shot, no kill basically! Garbage!
All it takes, is "slightly" crappy team members...and you're dead. There's no line of defense anymore, it's too hard to maintain and takes away from the game play. A couple monsters jump in your Defense line, and break it up, and everyone runs off....The AI also spawn WAY too smart! They pretty much spawn on TOP of you sometimes....incredibly annoying! It reminds me of Left 4 Dead...just incredibly stupid and annoying!!!
In KF1, it felt like you were Hunting...now in KF2, it feels like YOU are being hunted...and all the spawn points are controlled to box you in, on purpose. Also, another REALLY big problem, is the maps.....they are small!!! There's no open spaces anymore, nowhere to stand out in the field and stand "back-to-back" with you're buddies and mow down enemies, nowhere to Roam....terrible!!! It really pains me to give this a negative review, I absolutely LOVE KF1, still play it daily....but it MUST be said!!! KF2 has all the impressive graphics and action and speed of modern gaming, but lacks the pure team-play and exploration factor of KF1. Say what you want, but it's just Not the same...

- Loot is rewarding and fun to obtain
- It is a nice difficulty with it being hard enough but not impossible
- Animations and cut scenes were amazing to watch and see
- Story was very involving and progress felt earned and visible
- Bug free
- VOICE ACTING IS AMAZING
- Bosses are creative and fun to beat
- Only $15 on sale which is a steal!
Cons:
- Tutorial throws alot of information at you, but it is not terrible
- Lots of dialogue (if you don't like that)
Overall: 9/10 - Very high potential

Wow! Just wow!
This game is so good, I had to write my first ever review about it^^
On first sight, the rather unusual papercut aesthetic looks a bit weird and, together with the you-can-only-move-along-a-fixed-path-mechanic, might give the impression of a silly game with rather light mechanisms.
But thats so not the case. The graphics are spot on and convey just the right mood and atmosphere. Its very much like Diablo in that regard, just a tiny bit more funny.
Contrary to that, the mechanics couldn't be more different. Although still a hack'n'slash dungeon crawler, the way to go about your business is very different and refreshingly new.
Just to name a few:
-inside a dungeon you can only move along a fixed path from junction to junction (although the levels a randomly generated).
-shielded enemies have an actual shield icon somewhere near them, that you have to destroy first before you can damage them.
-gold and health pickups are gathered automatically once you hover your mouse over them.
-random(?) boss monsters have various stages where they use different skills.
-skills from regular monsters (like teleporting or summoning minions) can be cancelled by clicking on them.
Granted, those things make the game sound like some mobile clicker game, but it is not! Its difficult to explain, but as soon as everything is in motion, the game plays very smooth and tactically challenging while still being fast and (once you got used to the unusual ways of controlling) easy at the same time.
About the card mechanics... Don't assume, there is a card game mechanic here. Its just that skills/spells/items are represented as cards. They are equipped on a shared skillbar and can either be passive, activatable for mana or activatable for a specific amount of times before they need to be recharged.
I know I haven't covered all aspects of the game, like the wonderful random dungeon generation with a "learning" time prediction to make the game last exactly as long as you want it to.
This game offeres many new mechanics that at the same time tie in very well to the gameplay we are used to from previous dungeon crawlers. Granted, I've just played one of the three characters for about 90 minutes, but at this point the game feels very polished and I can't wait to see what the devs have up their sleeves for the coming months.
If you like dungeon crawl hack'n'slays - buy it!
If you are interested in cool new mechanics - buy it!

Early Access review
This is about the gameplay and not about the lag problems as i am certain they will solve. The lag problems are detailed in several posts and it might all be solved before you have read this post.
Gameplay review
-respawning
respawn just happens and they attack right away. you can get overwhelmed when followed by mobs / attacking and respawning. Not always an issue, but dying because you walk into a respawn area... reviving on the spot is possible. but you need to have a scroll (purchaseable). reviving on the nearest rez loc ... costs no xp but damages your gear. (repairing... need hammer (purchaseable). respawn in town (free -  possible long distance to travel)
- item stats
stats on some weapons are just weird. a two handed staff with a bonus for a dagger. a shield with stats for 2 handed sword. that kind of thing.
-open world
it's quite a linear thing. very narrow path. i have played up to level 15 and its ... very linear. there is only one path to follow. There are side branches. but it still feels reailroaded. like a bad written dunegons and dragons storyline.
-dungeons
dungeons are random generated and yet i feel like i did the same dungeon a few times. sometimes its hard to aim and run around with ranged weapons.
-story. 1/10
wait what? there is a story? no. there isn't. (not according to my book of storywriting)
-graphics 6/10
you cant rotate around your character on screen like you can in umbra/wolcen. The colors are good and the characters can look amazing. you can zoom in and look at your character.
-motion capture
the characters have a nice look and feel when they run. some effects look nice but the game doesn't give you the same combat experience like grim dawn does. i never played diablo 3 so cant compare to that game.
-combat
i am not sure what to think of it. I am no powerplayer and i do not min/max in depth. So far i did not have the same amount of fun with combat as i had with grim dawn.
there seems to be a slight delay between attack and action on screen. (the server is  currently in taiwan)
weapons:
it doesnt matter what weapon you have. The weapons just are things with stats and the look and feel can be changed with the garderobe. so its a stat-compare use what you like thing. Add a gun to the gardrobe (needs additional blue $$$ - can be earned in game time? not sure)
-skills
so far weapons found in the game do just add basic stats. then the skill makes your character do something. So there is definetly a game thought behind it, like:
use a 2h offense weapon (slow/dmg)
use a 1h/1h offense/offense weapon (fast/dmg)
use a 1h/1h offence/defence weapon (fast/tank)
range is added by skills. add a skill with 5 m frontal arc range (one of the rangers skills) and you have a bow that does not work like a bow. Weapons effectivly only change base stats, runes added to them only add bonus stats/improvements and the point selection  for skills make the character.
How you like your animation ... well. thats up to you. I am a gunner and can go for the dual wielder look with the clothing system while actually using a gun and a shield.
the immortal outfit actually looks quite nice.
-solo playability
when you pay attention to your build and select the right gear it is very well playable.
-group playability
not sure. i have not yet been able to join a group. as everybody is still in a hurry to show they are the mightiest of the mighty and no time to wait for a silly old fool that gets himself into trouble. (with the respawns)
-quests
finally... quests. there are quests. but as you might find with a non existent storyline they are very similar and very grinding of nature. It's a hack 'n slash so i can live with that.
I find the marking systems easy to use when the quest is inside the area, but difficult to follow when in town (with multiple portals.)
-events
lots of repeating events. repeating seems to be rewarded as you can get achievements for repeating them. are they fun? i dunno. i did a good number of them to gain XP. but thats it.
-replayability:
it's not very compelling to do again. When you have created and leveled one char it feels no different when you do it a second time. The character may have different skills.
the dungeons are random generated, but... they have a very similar touch and feel. so far i did not see or feel differnt biomes. (snow, desert, wet etc. or dark, hellish etc.)
PROS:
buy once (with a price of around 20 euro its very neat.)
the devs are reading, responding and listening.
graphics are good, not spectacular. lighting feels a little flat.
player housing
ticketing system: so far i got a real response on my ticket.
CONS:
settings do not work properly. this is a known problem: settings must be manually done in a config.
ingame purchase (you can play those rewards free or easy access buy them)
many areas are blocked / locked with unpassable object.
final verdict: 6/10
not bad for a 2016 release. However as some of the other players said: its not as good as some others. it doesn't look 2016 and there are some odd things.
there are certainly some interesting things going on here. but it isn't there yet. It's early access and prone to have bugs on different levels.
would i reccomend it... well if you are curious and want to know for yourself: feel free. 20 euro isn't too much. and gameplay will get better.
if you dont like early access games with bugs and oddities i would not recommend it. Then you have to wait.
for an EA game i say its worth the money.

This might be the best superhero game.  It's my favorite LEGO game.  If you're a Marvel fan, this is stuffed to the brim with characters and settings both familiar and obscure and the story is both amusing and clever.  It does a pretty great job of giving you a wide variety of super powers to play with, and, unlike LEGO Batman 2, doesn't make you wade through a dozen story missions to get to the good ones.  There are a ton of characters here and enough variety in how they play to make them really feel worth unlocking.
Flying (or gliding, or swinging, or ice-sliding, or goblin-gliding, or hovering, or driving) around the city is great fun.  Only DC Universe Online does a better job of capturing the feel of moving like a superhero.

As usual many reviews are negative because the game presents numerous problems on day one output in Early Access, not even to consider them.
Other reviews, however, are negative because each has its good reasons and there may be.
But others are bad because some users expect to find a Hack'n Slash like Diablo 3, Grim Dawn, Torchlight 2 etc.
Guardians Of Ember is a MMOARPG that the gameplay of Hack'n Slash but above all the style and settings of an MMORPG.
Its a great mix of both categories, and despite being in Early Access is coming on quite well.
In the game you will face the usual things we are used to in the MMORPG, but with the gameplay of a Hack'n Slash.
Before buying the game remember this, is not a pure ARPG or a pure MMORPG, but rather a great mix of both.
If you buy the game thinking that is still in Early Access and that is a MMOARPG, then you will find yourself in front of an almost unique game in its genre, and you will enjoy it for sure.
Recommended for lovers of the two categories.

Fantastic game.  I would say this is my personal favorite in the series for several reasons.  I'll keep this as spoiler free as possible just on a side note.  #1 The combat is the most polished in the series with extra things being added like environment takedowns.  #2 It is the most difficult game in the series combat wise and puzzle wise.  #3 the batmobile is a great addition even though it's a bit slow.  #4 The cinematics/psychological exploration of Bruce Wayne's mind of the game are the best in the series from my perspective.  #5 They added more obsure and interesting villians from the comics.  #6 Finally, this doesn't really apply to a comparison with Asylum, but of the open world Batman games this one felt more coherent, meaning a lot of stuff didn't feel as fetch quest like with the obvious exception of Riddler and one or two of the other side quests like City and Origins felt (meaning I actually was interested in every part of most of the side quests, not just the end).  However, I can say people may not like the lack of proper boss fights in this game.  They still exist, but they are not as prominent as any of the other games (ie Poison Ivy (Arkham Asylym) and Mr. Freeze (Arkham City)).  Overall, the most complete and best open world Batman game.
