The only reason I own Super Hexagon is because my good buddy bought it for me on sale. After it finished installing, I opened it up just to give it a shot. It took me a little off guard at first because it was bright and loud and weird, and the gameplay was... boring. The music was fun for the most part, and the little narrator voice was not as grating as others seem to think it is, but it didn't quite grip me like Dark Souls or I Wanna Be the Guy... That is until I got home from a particularly "meh" day. I booted up my computer to escape to the Internet, but then I noticed Super Hexagon on my desktop. Instinctively, I opened it up and began playing. This time seemed different than the others... I zoned out as the repetitive music and colors blended into one and I almost began to meditate. I was focused on one thing: keeping that triangle safe. Weirdly enough, lessons began to reveal themselves to me:
1. Go with the flow, but do not be afraid to go against it if you feel it's the better option
2. Take risks
3. Failure is not the end
4. Think on your feet
5. You don't always have to move to be safe
Now I have founded a church based off of Super Hexagon. We meet regularly on Tuesday evenings to discuss the meaning of life, love, and the origins of the little triangle of hope.
In conclusion, I want you all to remember that if you feel like you are not in control of your life, you can play this game. You will become responsible for the life of a little triangle and it is your job to keep it safe, and if you do fail, it will forgive you. ALL HAIL THE TINY TRIANGLE!
10/10 would buy again

What can I say about Resident Evil: Revelations 2 that has not been said already... It's okay, but heavly flawed both gameplay and story wise.
First off, the graphics are subpar at best, nothing fancy, but graphics don't mean everything in gaming, well to me anyways, so I will let that slide.
Now for the story, it is a very interesting and creepy story, but it doesn't allow much room to exand upon unfortunately, as for the characters, you have Claire Redfeild, Moria Burton for one half and Barry Burton and Natalia for the other and they both play pretty similar, but with some minor differences, which I will get to in a minute. First, Claire and Moria's half of the story is much better in my opinion simply because of the atmosphere, it's creepy, dark and you feel danger all around you, you don't get that or much of that from Barry and Natalia's half sadly, which contains mostly Barry and his overpowered weapons like his Magnum and Assualt Rifle you get at the very start and when you start, it's pretty much the ame enviroments as it's set in the after the events Clarie and Moria went through (Sorry for the spoiler if you haven't played it already). But overall the gameplay is where it's at right? Wrong. It is almost identical in the style of RE: Revelations and RE6, sloppy and most of the time really boring. The scenery can be nice for brief moments, but the audio is once again amazing for Resident Evil standards anyways, the voice acting? Meh.
Now the story was okay at the start, but then it kind of throws a curve ball at some points where your scratching your head as to why am I here? Who is this person behid all of this? What happens with your braclet? Ahh yes, before I forget about it, the braclets... They seem to only have a subtle part in the overall story, meaning it has nothing to do with the story, it's mentioned about 4 - 5 times and that's pretty much it, no build-up with it and no answers, just never mentioned again. Isn't that nice?
Anyways, the game is okay, but for Resident Evil standards, especially as of late, it's okay, but I would rather play Resident Evil 6 to be honest. That's right... I said it... This game is for real fans of Resident Evil or Third-Person Shooter fanatics, but not for the folks who liked anything between RE1 to RE4.

From all the hype I heard when I went into this game I was expecting an epic trilogy.  I didn't get that, I got saturday morning cartoon.
The first thing to understand is that due to the engine chosen it's not quite the open world you might have been spoiled with by modern RPGS. Rather it's a linear series disjointed micro levels that string thmselves to gethre to form a greater narrative. The moment you complete a map object you're teleported to a cutscene instance or to your next microlevel, Sidequests do exist, but only in the form of a  couple bonus levels that can easily be missed and that offer but offer nothing more than a half hour of game length, a couple thousand (redundant) currency, and some lore to fill out the universe.  None of them seemed pertinent to the character or the narrative and none of them had any greater lasting consequence.
The second thing to understand is that while some of those micro do a very good job of evoking a film noir detective feel, and while others are alright at making you feel like a cyberpunk badass, and that together they evoke a pen and paper game with a dungeon master and dice there were none that evoked a challenging game feel. As in the game was very easy. I played on hard and opted to scrimp and save at first on the optional mercenaries by going into levels only 2-3 runners instead of a possible four (there's only a couple NPCs of note so that rest of 4 man squad is filled out by hired grunts) and I still less deaths than I've had serious crushes.  And all that scrimping and saving? Completely unnecessary. I could buy all the best of everything by two thrids of the way through. Even the aforemention film noir detective moments which to expand upon took the form of exactly two logic I was very impressed with, well turns out they both can be bypassed by simpler brute force approaches. Actuallly, come to think of it, most of the game can be one simply  by having an appropriate amount of stat points. They'll even highlight all the of instant win options in green or red for you so you know which stats to get.
The third and final thing  to understand about Shadowrun Returns is the sixish hour campaign you get with the game is only the first episode of the saturday morning cartoon as the chosen engine when coupled with an apparently simple editor means amount of fan made content is both extensive and expanding.  I haven't yet tried any of it myself, but Sturgeon's Law must surely dictate that SOME of it is good.

A good roller coaster ride full of spoops. Has outright flawless environments and tension. I go back to this game every halloween to replay it and each time I still feel extremely tense when moving through. The payoff from all the tension is usually a garbage jump scare though. or no actual scare and instead a loud screech from the music indicating something spoopy is happening, you just weren't looking at it.
Aside from a few easily fixed technical issues the problems are near perfect. When I first played I noticed the choked fov and insane mouse acceleration... but only when not aiming. then it hit me, these are pseudo tank controls! They took the tension Resi 4 had with its tank controls and transplanted it into a modern action game. The controls don't feel sticky per-se but they feel deliberately slow in areas that matter. Sprinting feels cathardic. Not quite like how sprinting in resi felt like you were a moving train. but starting and stopping has this weight to it. not to mention during a sprint you can only really move straight ahead. These controls are built to make you take your time. to slowly walk through a hallway with your cutter out, or risk getting jumped on and taking damage.
Gameplay wise it's really good. The game's not afraid to throw crowds your way or drop an enemy on you in crowded areas. It oftens combines both of these making combat very tense. Instead of aiming for the head, you dismember enemies for extra damage, offering much more variety in enemy design and gameplay. there's weapons that take advantage of this, the starting plasma cutter is one of these. But there are still traditional hitscan shooty shoots like the pulse rifle. Every weapon has an alternate fire and there's plenty for everyone (except snipers, see Dead Space 2). Aside from the tension in fights the rock your seat spooks are very weak. except the one and only part where a necromorph jumps you after using an upgrade bench. That was awesome...
The difficulty can range from ok, to growingly frustrating. I played dead space a few times on both hard and normal. Hard mode is the better of the two, with the difficulty adding more tension to fights providing more genuine scares from the gameplay itself. But becomes very frustrating as you'll fight literal bullet sponge black variants of the same enemies you've fought for the past few hours. And with the game being a survival horror with no ability to dodge monster encounters you end up strategizing in the form of buying as much ammo for the most effecient weapons you have. When the game throws these bullet sponges at you however you end up gravitating to your first weapon, the plasma cutter, more often. Since it's very ammo effecient, does great damage to necromorphs and you'll often upgrade it first before you get a better weapon. Normal doesn't have this, thankfully. But it lacks the tension in the gameplay. killing the replay value
New game+ does not relieve this issue. since it keeps your gear and outright spoils you with a tanky suit upgrade and 50,000 credits. It gets rid of some of the annoyance of fighting tanky crowds of enemies. But you're comparatively so overpowered it hardly matters.
Great game though. It's always a game I come back to and enjoy. So it's among some of my favourite games. pick it up for its current price or on sale. but I guess I recommend buying for the lowest price. It's not like visceral's getting any money off this game anymore...

This is by far my favorite game in the series. If you like the older resident evil games, or any of the silent hill games, this game is for you. Even with full and easy control of your character, the game STILL manages to be super creepy.
Here are some things you WON'T find in this game:
- QTE's
- Boulder punching
- Spamming a button to pull yourself up a ledge on the final boss fight
- Steroids
- Huge mobs of zombies
- Enemies riding motorcycles and firing guns
- Huge♥♥♥♥♥♥br>- Boob physics
Is it groundbreaking? No. Is it as bad as everyone says it is? No. I honestly don't see the hate around this game. It's just REV1 with every last drop of CoD siphoned out. I like resident evil for the atmosphere, and the environments. I'm also not a fan of fixed camera angles, so keep that in mind as well. In my opinion, this and RE4 are the two best RE games currently out there (RE Remake would be second best).
Pros:
- Amazing atmosphere and visuals
- Interesting enemies and bosses
- Limited ammo and supplies
- Stealth missions
- Companions don't get in the way as much as say, Ashley
- Companions also aren't completely worthless
- Characters aren't roided out or shoving their♥♥♥♥♥♥and♥♥♥♥♥down your throat
- Characters react realisticly to the situation at hand
- No QTEs (except when a monster grabs you, then you must shake the mouse)
- Solid controls
- Inventory management and combining
- The inventory system is easy to use and navigate
- Skill trees for upgrading your characters in the story mode
- Creepy as♥♥♥♥♥♥br>- It's just really fun
- Interesting story and character development
- Raid mode is very arcade-y, but is doesn't try to be anything else
- Raid mode has a bunch of maps from RE6
- Raid mode has two-player COOP
- Offline campaign coop
- An absolute ♥♥♥♥-ton of stuff to unlock (figures, concept art, challenge mode things, weapons, etc)
- Challenge mode thing for levels (all enemies invisible, time limit, etc)
- Decisions in the past affect the future
Cons
- No online campaign (but there is an offline coop campaign)
- When I first load a level my CPU usage maxes out for a bit, killing the framerate and causing frequent jitters and freezes (doesn't happen to everybody, and goes away after a minute or so)
- Companions can sometimes get hung up on enemies, but I have yet to have a companion actually die from an enemy
- Mouse input could be smoother
- Really bad lip-sync in-game, but not noticable unless you always look at characters' faces when they speak
- Lots of hackers in raid-mode (although if playing with friends only, there isn't much of a difference)
- You have to unlock things and also buy them with BP (in-game currency), could be frustrating for some
- More enemy types would be nice, but there are still way more than REV1.

Overall, as a hardcore resident evil fan, I think the game was good enough for me to give it a thumbs up.  Don't expect the world but expect a decent resident evil experience.

An incredibly fun, yet punishing top-down space simulator.
Upon entering, you'll find that you are the last hope of the Federation, carrying vital information key to crippling the Rebellion. On your first few playthroughs, you'll be lucky to get past the first few sectors, but the hopes of unlocking different ships or variations of what you already have beckons you to press on.
Until, at long last, salvation! You've made it to 'The Last Stand' -- The final sector of the game, you encounter the Rebel Flagship for the first time, and you are decimated by it. This process repeats, each time you learn more and more about this seemingly impossible adversary. Then finally! Success!! You destroy the monstrosity... But, wait... It didn't explode, it just jumped away... OH FOR ♥♥♥♥S SAKE!!
You fight the flagship once more, but with it's power now altered to drones. Ultimately, the damage you took from your first run is your undoing, and you fail once more.
Trying and trying again, you finally defeat the flagship's demonic drone phase, only to find it has one final form for you to face off against. Surely you're capable enough to fell the beast, right?
Wrong. In a blaze of blood, sweat and tears, you are destroyed.
Everything seems hopeless, you want to give up, you feel your sanity slipping. But you must kill this ship. You need to save the Federation.
Painstakingly, you try more and more, until you finally discover a combination that works. Wether it be brute force, or just a clever intrication of teleporters, bombs and lasers, you bring the flagship to it's final square of hull. You pause your game triumphantly as you fire the last laser, savouring the moment. But all good things must come to an end... You hit spacebar and watch as the flagship crumbles, when you realise... You forgot to teleport your crew back, and now only your pilot is alive to celebrate... ♥♥♥♥... And did I mention that was just 'Easy' mode?
Great game, great soundtrack, intricate backstory and dialogues. One thing still irks me though;
Over the course of 250 attempts, I've killed the flagship only 10 times...
10/10 would die again.

Faerie Solitaire is not your stereotypical solitaire game. Rather than having seven distinct piles of cards which you are trying to put in order, you are instead trying to clear the board. This is done by discarding cards from the table which are within one of the top card in the discard pile. To further spice this up there are special rules and conditions. Most of these involve locking some of the cards until you empty another row or play a specific card.
The game includes an element of collecting and leveling as well. You receive gold, resources, and eggs while you play. Gold is the only thing which has a direct effect on game play as it allows you to buy various bonuses, like undos, to make the game a little easier. The eggs and resources are simply fluff which add to the story.
Yes, I said story.
This game is driven by a relatively simple story line. You are trying to save the faeries! They use this to justify the different levels, objectives, and added complexity. Each level consists of several chances to meet some objective like combo length, gold earned, or achieving a perfect game within a specified amount of time.
The episodic nature led me to keep playing until well past when I should go to sleep. I found myself wanting to finish a level, or see what the next challenge was, or just finish leveling up my pet...
Overall the game is a satisfying solitaire experience.

This is a fantastic turn based RTS that I heavily recommend.
-Nice variety of units, civs, benefits, and management (resources, tiles, money, science, etc)
-Several different ways to play each civ. Most are good at two or three victory routes.
-Mechanics like science and culture bend to your playstyle more than you bend to their limitations.
-Maps are randomly generated, but never feel unbalanced or unplayable.
-The DLC bundle is only $50, and really enhances the game experience.
I consider this to be a mid to high strategy focused game. It has far more depth than your average strategy game, but can't compare to something like EU (which isn't turn based).
There are some slight issues.
-Some civs (ie Japan, Russia) are clearly better than others.
-Team battles with AI partners can be an upredictable experience. They declare war, you march your army to the enemy, they negotiate peace, then they declare war on an enemy that's next to your capital but your whole army is across the map... Thanks, AI.
-You can have some pretty awful start locations. Start in the center of a desert, a civ to your north and south, ocean east and west, and only incense and iron? Have fun with that!
-Gandhi. I shall never again trust you and your war mongering ways.
There are some ways to overcome the game. For example, building on tundra or desert limits your city's potention. Building on snow literally gives it no potential. Great engineers, merchants, and scientists can construct on all but water tiles, making even snow tiles productive.
All in all, 10/10 with all DLC. If you're hesitant, get the bundle on sale. It's worth $50; it's theft at $10. :)

I can't honestly recommend this game. It's not a bad game - far from it. It's very well put together. The graphics are beautiful, the controls are polished, and the overall production is top notch. If wanted a prettier Arkham game with all the dials turned to 11, this is it.
Plot wise, it's a bland mish-mash of multiple graphic novels -- I won't mention them here as not to spoil it, but somehow, Arkham Knight manages to muddle them together into something resembling a plot. There's a lot of other Batman references/characters inserted into the game, too, which also winds up being a confused mess. You'll complete a major plot point only to have Alfred pop up and tell you that the Riddler/Manbat/Two Face/Azrael/Mad Hatter (who for all intents and purposes is a better dressed Riddler)/Flying fire boy are up to no good and need to be taken care of.
Gameplay-wise.... Batmobile, the goddamn Batmobile. You spend about a third of the game inside of it, and it's not bad... but after a few missions it simply stops being fun and becomes another chore for you to finish before you can get to the good parts. Grappling through the city, fighting mooks, and sneaking around are where the series shines, and replacing that gameplay with 'just ok' tank/driving sections was a poor design decision. Combat is the same old Arkham Combat, complete with the annoying shield/knife/electrified enemies. Things get interesting when you get to play as other characters, but opportunities to do so are rare and are over far too soon.
If you loved Arkham Asylum and Arkham City, and you really want more of the same thing, Knight is a good bet. There's a lot for fans of the character and the game series in here. Otherwise, it's just a mix villians  and random missions loosely held together by a muddled plot and really hurt by repetitive and boring vehicle combat.

With plenty of ways to play the game (class, weapons, armour), plenty of things to explore/do.
The game is a solid 7-8/10 on its own, but for anyone who's watched South Park, I would go as far as rating it 9/10. Not perfect, but there's just so much here that is great that I would've never expected for them to put in or remember.

While the game does have the familiar TBS feel of its predecessors I can't help but feel the game didn't quite live up to the expectations or potential that it certainly had. The campaign seems a bit short and the customization options just aren't there. Perma-death is still something that happens (hey you're engaging an alien force that for most of the game seems to have superior weapons and technology) but that makes you have to think about your moves and not just charge into the unknown. It just feels as though they've taken a step back from Apocalypse.
All in all still a pretty good game and if you enjoy TBS games then you'll get some fun out of this one more than likely. If you're a fan of the franchise you'll probably end up feeling as I did: disappointed at the potential not being utilized.
Recommended if you're a big TBS fan, otherwise wait until it's on sale.

Many young people growing up, think gaming is just play. It's more then that, and this is what Free To Play shows. It's an insightful look into the world of DOTA 2, showing the human element that's forgotten.
When I explained to my parents during the last International, they couldn't believe that so much money was at stake. Just like your parents, mine were in the same boat saying "Those games aren't going any good. Go study."
Maybe it's due to the fact that they had to work hard against their peers, or that they don't realize that gaming is becoming the next big thing (both playing the game and the developmental work). It could even be the two factors together.
As you will see in this video, these pro level players are normal people. And just like a physical sport, mental sports have a place in the world. The most important part is, the generation that's growing up will realize that sports don't have to mean football, soccer, rugby, and basketball. These aren't nerds who like computing Pi. These featured individuals are connectable, which is why E-Sports may take over the physical sports one day.
People fall into the trap where they spend their whole life playing games. Free to Play shows that just like any other career or sport, you have to make sacrifices. In some cases they are family, work, and even education. Don't forget however, gaming requires the people to develop the title over time. That is where I think Valve should go next. What is it like to make a title such as DOTA 2?
As Free To Play isn't a game, I can't hand it a normal rating. So all I'm going to say is, if you are a gamer out there, you have to watch this. It doesn't matter if you play DOTA 2 or not, it really shows the life of the people you may look forward to being one day.

First off, before writing this review, I have to make mention of the quality of the port and how to improve it. There are two major issues, first off; the atrocious mouse controls (due to being tied to the game's performance, fix this by downloading the Dead Space MouseFix mod found here:
and secondly; the downright BROKEN physics (somehow caused by vSync, turn it off and force in console).
Now you've got the game working though, a more important question arises: "is it worth playing" to that, I'd say the answer is a resounding yes.
To elaborate, the game's systems and setting combine in such a way as very few games can achieve, the clunkinkess of Isaac Clarke's movement, combined with the cramped corridoors and other such locations of the USG Ishimura play off one another almost perfectly and constantly bolster the atmosphere already established by genuinely unique body horror visuals and absolutely stellar sound design (seriously play this game with surround sound headphones, it really changes the entire experience for the better).
In terms of gameplay, you're going to be switching between combat and puzzles rather frequently, and while the puzzles can be something of a mixed bag in terms of quality,, and do get somewhay samey towards the end, they at least build on established mechanics thoughout the entire game, ranging from slowing objects, to manipulating physics, to traversing zero-gravity environments and so forth. The combat, however, really stands on it's own, having a to-this-day unique system based entirely around dynamic dismemberment that can be used in multiple ways, for example, removing an enemy's leg to slow it down while you focus on others, as well as challenging conventions you will have gotten used toi from having played other games (such as aiming for headshots) it really feels interesting an fresh - even 9 years later. with 7-8 different weapons that all feel great to use  from your usual pistol and assault rifle stand-in's (all weapons hold an industial mining theme) to more unique tools, such as the ripper; a contraption that shoots out spinning saw blades and suspends them in mid-air so you can dismember as you please, all of which have multiple upgrade paths to take, as well as the aforementioned physics manipulation and slow-motion mechanics adding a couple more layers of depth to the combat, enemy designi also plays heavily into the combat system, as they always have limbs that can be removed to slow them down, as well as dismemberment being the quickest way to defeat any enemy in the game..
The story, while nothing to write home about (think Alien with zombies) does have a few interesting twists and turns throughout, which I will not spoil here.
Dead Space absolutely excells as an action game, but as a horror games, I'd argue it is even stronger. Due almost entirely to the sound design, which will always add unnerving chatter and ambient noises of she ship, such as metal scraping on metal, or clanging sounds coming from dark corners as well as the screechse and shrieks that can be heard frmm the game's line-up of enemies, all of which have uniquely distinguishable sounds that aren't shared with other enemies, these aspects, combined with the excellent 5.1 audio mixing are the gane's strongest aspects, both in it's attempt at horror, and the overall atmosphere that the game sets out to achieve.
tl;dr good game, do play

FTL or Faster Then Light is a indie kick started game by Subset Games, In which you play as a space ship captain tasked with getting the secret plans of how to defeat the Death Star sorry I mean Enemy Mother Ship to the rest of you fleet while being cased by the rebel fleet. The game  is different as all of the systems and events are randomly generated so no one with have the same experience though life is hard in this galaxy with permadeath and may a foe you will die may times by this part of the experience and increases the replay ability of this game which you could get through in about thirty minutes.
The game is played for a top down real time strategy view with you being able to pause at anytime to assign tasks to your crew as you mange your shields, engines, weapons, oxygen, airlocks and many other systems. Other then the combat their will be may choices you have to make from spending your hard fought scrap on repairing your ship, getting better shields or that cool new Perseus missile launcher. As well as dialog choices similar to a choose your own adventurer story with the all powerful Blue opinions in may  cases if you have a type of crew, weapons or module.
The game features 7 unique races with the plain humans, the mechanical Engi who are good at repairing, the violent Mantis who like nothing more than to rip you limb for limb, the Rockmen who laugh off fire, the powerful Zoltan with the ability to add more power to your systems, the ancient crystal the ancestors of the rock men and the traitorous slugs with their telepathic abilities.
The music by Ben Prunty is split into two distinct styles the peaceful and calming low key music when you drifting in space and readying your ship for the next jump into the unknown, Contrasting the fast paced, heart pumping battle music which adds so much stress and tension to the intense battle management.
Overall FTL is a great unique indie title with brilliant design and hours of fun to be had here.

Now, to start off, I'm fairly seasoned when it comes to games that mess with your head a little bit. Of course, there are games with changing environments and odd paths that you don't recognise, and we play these out pretty well, we solve the puzzles with a relative amount of ease and get through the game at a good pace.
And then there's Antichamber.
From the start of Antichamber, I was a bit thrown off by the fact it does not really have a main menu screen. I was sat staring at my monitor waiting for something to load for about 5 minutes before I moved my mouse and realised I was already in the game. When I did eventually turn around, I was faced with a map with one room on it, which I clicked and was instantly teleported there.
Now, I don't want to spoil anything, so I'm just going to say that the rooms are confusing and you don't know where you're going half the time. This is definitely not a bad thing, as the main point of the game is to get lost exploring the Antichamber, desperately searching for the coveted exit door, which is always out of reach. There are times where the game will make it so that you have to restart from the map, but you will have all the areas you have already been to unlocked, so you can start from where you please.
All in all, this is a puzzle game unlike any other, it's unique qualities truly make it stand out from the other games out there. On occasion, it will make you angry with yourself for taking the same path 6 times without realising, but the adaptive qualities of the rooms and the entire map make this game so very special.
Antichamber gets in at 97% out of 100% for me, as it is truly a game that any player needs to experience to find it truly amazing. But be warned, it is confusing as hell at times.

Resident Evil: Revelations 2 is a good game and if you are a fan of Resident Evil you will certainly enjoy the ride. Revelations 2 takes place between RE5 and 6 and ties in strongly to the main story arche of the series. Without any spoiler I will say the events will effect future titles. It was done very well and ties up a few loose ends.
Revelations 2 puts the player in the shoes of two fan favorite characters, Claire Redfield and Barry Burton (star characters from the first two games) who each has their respective partner. Claire has Barry's daughter Moira Burton as her partner and Barry has the mysterious new charater Natalia to accompany him. Claire and Barry will handle the majority of the action while Moira and Natalia will provide much needed support. You can swap between both the main and support character at anytime during the game while the AI will control the other character (think RE0 if you have played that before). The combat is extremely fluid and very addicting once you get the hang of character swapping.
Speaking of combat, this is not RE6. The ammo in this game is far more scarce and you must stun an enemy before you can melee (much like re4 and 5). You will want to use your ammo wisely to make sure you do not run out, which will happen if you go in blazing. A new feature in this game is an MMO style skill system that you can level up with Battle Points you earn for completing chapters. This allows you to specialize your character in certain areas to make them more effecient to your playstyle. If you are a fan of this costumization system you can look forward to spending many hours in Raid mode after completing the main story. In this mode you can choose between many different characters and level them up in a dungeon style setting while acquiring new weapons and skills along the way.
A few of the settings in the game are unsettling, especially the prison where the game begins. However several of the areas can become bland fast and this is one of the games true weak spots. There are some very unique enemies, however there is not a large variety. The Revenants will surely creep you out when you first meet them.
~To sum up; If you are a fan of Resident Evil you should buy this game. It has a very relevant story and some long missed characters. It has a much stronger focus on the survival aspect than more recent titles in the series. The lack of enemy variety and the bland scenery are the most obvious downsides. You do get a lot of content for the price of the game, especially if you plan on sinking time into the bonus modes.~

This is not pew-pew-pew action combat. The ships are lumbering behemoths like in Star Trek, where the strategic choices you make determine the outcome of combat.
Do you shoot missiles to bust out the ship's shield systems? Will you focus on laser fire against the weapons instead?
Or you will take chances and warp your crew and attempt to board the enemy ship for a larger bounty - at the risk of losing some of your crew?
Each playthrough has random maps generated, so you never know what lies ahead of you.
The incoming rebel fleet adds a sense of urgency and does not allow the player to fully explore a sector, and there are secrets out there to be found...
A single playthrough does not last very long, but there is always more to come back at: achievements, rare stuff to find, ship designs to unlock, different playstyles to go through.
And once you are done, there is a nascent modding community to keep you going even more.
Don't let the retro look deceive you, this is a HARD strategy game, for hardcore gamers.

The game has a lot of things going on, with a story that resembles 5-10 or so episodes (not in length, but in terms of plot). There are plenty of twists to keep things interesting. The characters are great -- your cast of South Park characters, some that will buddy with you. I spent about <20 hours, but played it to complete everything and see as many of the hidden secrets as I could. However, it could be completed a lot faster as some negative reviews point out, to which I say, many of the greatest games can be completed extremely shortly (including Chrono Trigger).
To continue with a comparison to Chrono Trigger (already something impressive), although it isn't as long or full of content if you play it to exhaustion, it is definitely a solid all around light RPG game. With plenty of ways to play the game (class, weapons, armour), plenty of things to explore/do.
The game is a solid 7-8/10 on its own, but for anyone who's watched South Park, I would go as far as rating it 9/10. Not perfect, but there's just so much here that is great that I would've never expected for them to put in or remember.

Dying light is what you get when you combine Mirror's edge and Dead island, then mix in a bit of Farcry.
As soon as load the game the graphics look very nice, and seem to be well optimized for high FPS.
The combat for the most part feels very fluid and fun, being able to chain hits together and decapitate multiple zombies with one handed weapons. Although early on in the game, you run out of stamina pretty quick from swinging a pipe around, so you might just want to stick to running around on rooftops untill you get better skills and gear.
I love the freerunning in this game, it feels very Mirrors edge-y. You can outrun common zombies (Biters) easily, so they aren't too threatening. The skill trees are nicely designed and, instead of choosing your favorite skill tree to put all your points into, you get skill points for the different trees by doing things related to them (eg. Climing to get agility points).
The crafting system is pretty generic, but it works. You can craft quite a variety of weapon mods that let you create some pretty cool looking weapons. In addition to weapons, you can also craft tools such as explosive shurikens, grenades, sheilds, ect. You'll learn how to craft new items as you level up.
You feel pretty safe in the day, what with there being few zombies that can chase you, but at night, the game changes from running rooftop to rooftop, looting, and killing weak zombies, to a stealth action game, where you hide from demonic spawn that can chase you down and rip you to pieces (Volatiles). However you do get double XP at night, giving you an insentive you stay out late.
Well overall, I'd say I really enjoy this game. I know this review dosn't cover everything in the game, but its just to give people an idea of what its like. If you like games like Farcry or Dead island, or maybe you're entertained by dropkicking zombies off of buildings of various hights, then I would recommend this game.

The art style seems a little cartoonish at times but there is an obvious lineage to the source material. The tactical combat more or less plays like fallout 2. What you can accomplish in a turn is determined by your action points. The character you can create looks the part, but SR vets will find the creation process bland and lacking in options. Shadowrun is a game full of weapons, spells, and cyberware. Your options here are so scant it will feel like a shaved down arcade version of the real thing.
Flaws aside, I had fun playing this game. It was definitely made in the spirit of Shadowrun by people who care about the IP. It may not be a successor to the Shadowrun throne but for now it's the next best thing.

Let me start by saying I'm hardly one for survial horror or shooters for that matter, but Dead Space and Dead Space 2 rank as two of my favorite games of all-time. I first played the games on PS3 before picking up copies on PC and for the most part Dead Space is the same game (for better or worse) across both platforms. Why do I love Dead Space so much if I dislike two of its core elements? In Dead Space you have a game aesthetic which captures two of my great loves Aliens and John Carpenter's The Thing. Add this to the fact that Dead Space takes a novel approach to shooting that adds a thrilling element of strategy and responsiveness and you've got a recipe for fun. The game takes full advantage of this by offering a variety of equally awesome weapons and the Rivet Gun, unique environments that fit the subject matter like a glove and awesome encounters. Another thing that makes Dead Space so awesome is the games sense of empowerment, yes there are scary bits but evey situation can be managed so long as you don't panic.
Beyond the gameplay design the sound design ranks amongst the best I've ever heard. While the game sounds excellent via Stereo output, in surround or through headphones the game audio is elevated to an entirely different level. This audio is major aspect of Dead Space's horror as everything you hear is in some way discomforting even Isaac's footsteps and breathing. While I've spent the majority of this review gushing over the game, there are some things I dislike about the title most specifically the PC port. It's a very mediocre port in my opinion, the PC controls feel sluggish and jittery at the same time which would seem impossible but somehow isn't. Against all reason this shooter plays better on PC with a controller. Navigating menu's is something of a chore as well, even with the controller the menus feel clunky and unresponsive. Then there are the characters, while I understand that the environment is supposed to be the true main character it would've been nice to have more. Isaac is a nothing man, just a hollow avatar through which the player experiences fear. The other two characters are a pair of panick stricken bickerers and even Nicole is left out to dry in terms of characterization. It would've have been nice to learn a little something about the various companions within the game but alas we were mostly left out to dry.
Dead Space in a nutshell is an awesome game that should scratch the itch for fans of shooters, horror and sci-fi alike. It provides memorable moments, cool weapons and one of the more unique settings in gaming. However as much as I love the game I struggle with whether or not to recommend it for the sole reason that this is an Electronic Arts published game. Despite my dislike of EA I am hesitant to punish a truly awesome game for shareholder tomfoolery. So ultimately I'm going to tell any curious persons to grab this one, it's a gem.

-Status effects work on bosses and MP damage can solve a fight or two. Both are refreshing changes from the norm.
A negative
-Some parts can be frustrating to figure out. I had 3, 2 of which I resorted to the net to navigate through but 1 of those was me being forgetful.
Questionable
-The plot itself is enjoyable but a number of twists can be easily seen coming. So easliy in fact and due to the nature of the game's writing I can't decide if they were actually meant to be running jokes and not twists.
-There are characters scattered about (and marked) that ask you to post reviews on steam and comments of somesort on facebook. I don't know if you're rewarded for doing so as I had no intention of writing a review until I had actually beaten the game. This made these NPCs slightly annoying whenever they popped up but since they were marked out it wasn't terrible. Their addition probably encouraged me to write a review after I was done with it but their 3 options of "Link to Steam Review", "Link to Facebook", and "I am a stupid meanie head" was not endearing. A simple request/reminder without the aggression in the dialogue to end the conversation would have been enough.
It should be mentioned what when the game says "Alt + Enter for full screen" it's refering to left Alt. Similar to the encouter autofight button which is left Ctrl. I mention this incase you want to build a script to help you farm pirate keys late game. (stupid pirate keys)
